ALS.summary: Livingston tells Jay to add six groups to his cipher: be 600, ce 601, de 602, fe 603, ge 604, he 605. Each is defined by spelling the syllable in two existing groups, the second always e (226).

snip.cap: Livingston’s draft: “Make this addition to your cypher”, six pairs of numbers, a syllable written under each
snip.credit: New-York Historical Society, R. R. Livingston Papers (EJ 1537), draft of 28 Nov 1781; photostat in Columbia University RBML, Jay Papers, ldpd:11572, via Columbia Digital Library Collections

system: Charles Thomson's printed 600-entry syllable-and-word nomenclator (WE007 family), in a copy numbered differently from Jay's; the line adds six new groups 600-605 for be, ce, de, fe, ge, he, each defined by spelling it in two existing groups.
